ActionLocationAssessment.description:
One evaluated snapshot: a driver/truck proximity verdict plus the
precinct-membership facts evaluated alongside it.

`frozen=True`: an assessment is a record of what was observed at
`evaluated_at` — mutating it after construction would let a caller silently
rewrite history. `extra="forbid"`: a field this contract does not know about
is a sign the wire format has drifted between backend and frontend, and
should fail loudly rather than pass through unnoticed.
ActionLocationAssessment.title: ActionLocationAssessment

AnchorStatus.description:
Hedera anchor state for one phase event. A phase may be
`completed` while its anchor is `failed` — that keeps the fail-open policy
honest, since the system still knows a receipt is owed. Never render `failed`
as success.
AnchorStatus.title: AnchorStatus

AnchoredField.description: A phase value checked against the payload its receipt committed.
AnchoredField.title: AnchoredField

AnchoredRecord.description:
One Hedera receipt plus the exact canonical string that was hashed, so a
verifier can hash that string itself instead of trusting our serialisation.
AnchoredRecord.title: AnchoredRecord

AssistantTurn.description: One earlier message, kept in the browser (spec D6): its text and the records it showed or meant.
AssistantTurn.title: AssistantTurn

AuditPackIssued.description: Returned once, at issue: the only time the raw share token exists anywhere.
AuditPackIssued.title: AuditPackIssued

AuditPackOptions.description: What the issuer chose to include — POPIA minimality is decided per pack.
AuditPackOptions.title: AuditPackOptions

Basis.description: One tool call an answer rests on: which tab, which dates, how many closed trips.
Basis.title: Basis

BlockchainReceiptRead.description:
Full receipt shape returned by blockchain endpoints and embedded in TripDetailResponse.

Uses subject_type/subject_id rather than the legacy trip_id field so that
receipts for vehicles, drivers, and events can all be represented uniformly.
BlockchainReceiptRead.title: BlockchainReceiptRead

BusyEntry.description: One driver, horse or trailer, and the trip that has it in the asked-about window.
BusyEntry.title: BusyEntry

CancelTripRequest.description:
POST /trips/{trip_id}/cancel body. note is required — a dispatcher abandoning a
trip mid-plan without stating why is the single most audit-sensitive gap this action
could leave. RequiredFreeText, not a bare min_length, also rejects invisible-char-only notes.
CancelTripRequest.title: CancelTripRequest

CancellationsBucket.description: Chart 1.7: trips that ended in this bucket, and how many of those were cancelled.
CancellationsBucket.title: CancellationsBucket

CancelledTrip.description:
One row of chart 1.7's table. The cancellation note is not carried here: it lives
inside a free-text exception description, so the table links to the trip page, which
shows it.
CancelledTrip.title: CancelledTrip

ChatTurn.description:
One earlier message, as text only. Kept in the browser, never on the server (spec D7).
The browser could send anything here, which is harmless: it only shapes the caller's own
answer, and the tools take the organisation from the token, never from the conversation.
ChatTurn.title: ChatTurn

ChooseCard.description: Two or more records matched what was typed: each is a button that answers "which one?".
ChooseCard.title: ChooseCard

ConfirmationSummary.description: A submitted capture, without its evidence. An upload alone is never a confirmation.
ConfirmationSummary.title: ConfirmationSummary

ConsignmentManifest.description:
One consignment's slice of the manifest — multi-client trips return one per client
booking (FP-112). Grouping by consignment is what lets evidence be cut per client.
ConsignmentManifest.title: ConsignmentManifest

CostBucket.description: One week, month or year, by the first attested departure (as every fleet chart).
CostBucket.title: CostBucket

CostProfileRead.description: The rates in force for the caller's organisation, and where they came from.
CostProfileRead.title: CostProfileRead

CostProfileUpdate.description: An admin's change to the rates. Any field left out keeps its current value.
CostProfileUpdate.title: CostProfileUpdate

CrewResourceType.description: The three things a trip occupies. Ordered as the wizard asks for them.
CrewResourceType.title: CrewResourceType

CriticalWaiting.description: Critical problems waiting for a dispatcher's review, right now.
CriticalWaiting.title: CriticalWaiting

CustodyIntegrityRead.description: Dispatcher-only result of verifying the full custody chain.
CustodyIntegrityRead.title: CustodyIntegrityRead

DayBlock.description: A quarter of the South African day, for chart 3.5 (risky times of day).
DayBlock.title: DayBlock

DelayCost.description: Hours late at final arrival on trips that had a problem, at the delay rate.
DelayCost.title: DelayCost

DispatcherProfileRead.description:
The dispatcher's own profile for the portal: UserRead plus the organisation's display
name, so the UI never hardcodes whose dashboard it is showing.
DispatcherProfileRead.title: DispatcherProfileRead

DispatcherReviewOutcome.description:
The choices a dispatcher may actually submit — ExceptionReviewOutcome without
LEGACY_REVIEW, which is a migration-only marker no dispatcher should be able to pick
for a review happening today.
DispatcherReviewOutcome.title: DispatcherReviewOutcome

DriverCheckpointCreateBody.description:
Slim checkpoint-creation body for the driver endpoint — trip_id comes from the URL path.

Unlike CheckpointBase above (a read shape, which must echo whatever is already
stored), this is client input and carries the full constraint set: bounded strings,
and GPS ranges matching the ones TripExceptionBase already enforces. Both coordinate
pairs are a driver-supplied position on an evidence record, so an out-of-range value
is a 422, not a row that can never be plotted.
DriverCheckpointCreateBody.title: DriverCheckpointCreateBody

DriverContact.description:
What the other party may see of a driver: no identity number, licence number or
verification vendor data.
DriverContact.title: DriverContact

DriverCreateBody.description:
Fields the dispatcher submits when registering a new driver.

organization_id is injected from the dispatcher's JWT — not accepted from the client.
Constrained types (not bare `str`) because this is client input; read shapes above
stay unconstrained so they can echo rows that predate these rules.
DriverCreateBody.title: DriverCreateBody

DriverDetailResponse.description:
Extended driver shape returned by GET /drivers/{id}: event log, receipts, and
the IDs of trips assigned to this driver.
DriverDetailResponse.title: DriverDetailResponse

DriverExceptionCreateBody.description: Slim exception-creation body for the driver endpoint — trip_id comes from the URL path.
DriverExceptionCreateBody.title: DriverExceptionCreateBody

DriverLocationCapture.description:
The raw phone reading a driver submits for a non-persistent comparison.

This intentionally contains no verdict: preview and completion each evaluate
the raw capture afresh, so a previous preview can never authorize completion.
DriverLocationCapture.title: DriverLocationCapture

DriverMetricsResponse.description: One driver's closed-trip trends, with the driver's display name.

confirmation_dwell_minutes_avg.description: Not purely driver behaviour: a slow receiver at the destination also lengthens the gap between unloading and confirmation.
confirmation_dwell_minutes_avg.title: Confirmation Dwell Minutes Avg

exception_trip_rate.description: Share of trips that carried at least one exception.
exception_trip_rate.title: Exception Trip Rate

on_time_departure_rate.description: Strictly on or before plan, over trips that had a planned departure at all.
on_time_departure_rate.title: On Time Departure Rate

DriverMetricsResponse.title: DriverMetricsResponse

DriverParticipationHistoryRead.description:
What a known former (or current) participant may see of their own periods. No later
live tracker trail, other drivers' identity details, cargo manifest or exception stream.
DriverParticipationHistoryRead.title: DriverParticipationHistoryRead

DriverSubstitutionContextRead.description:
The ongoing-collection context for a pending incoming/outgoing driver. Stops and
findings reuse the existing driver-safe shapes rather than inventing parcel data.
DriverSubstitutionContextRead.title: DriverSubstitutionContextRead

DriverTripListItemResponse.description:
One row of GET /api/v1/trips/me — the authenticated driver's own trip list.

Deliberately not TripListItemResponse: that carries driver/horse/trailers a driver
already knows, and omits precinct names, which are resolved server-side here.
status is the coarse TripStatus the PWA groups its Active/Upcoming/Past tabs by;
the phase ledger, not this field, sequences the trip.
DriverTripListItemResponse.title: DriverTripListItemResponse

DriverUpdateBody.description:
Fields the dispatcher may change via PATCH /drivers/{id}; only supplied fields
apply. POPIA: license_number is accepted here but only its SHA-256 hash goes to Hedera.

Omissible is not the same as nullable, same convention as PrecinctUpdateBody
(schemas/organisations.py). test_patch_schema_nullability_matches_the_model pins
this against the SQLAlchemy model.
DriverUpdateBody.title: DriverUpdateBody

DurationStats.description: Distribution of one lane measure over the pooled observations. All values in minutes.
DurationStats.title: DurationStats

EmailCodeSent.description:
Where the code went, masked (j***@santam.co.za): the holder of a forwarded link
learns which inbox to ask about, not the full address.
EmailCodeSent.title: EmailCodeSent

EvidenceAnchorSummary.description:
Where one anchorable action on an exception stands. `pending` and `failed` are debts
the retry sweep owes; only `anchored` carries a receipt.
EvidenceAnchorSummary.title: EvidenceAnchorSummary

EvidenceArtifactWithUrl.description:
Dispatcher read shape: metadata plus a short-lived signed URL.

A subclass, not a field on EvidenceArtifactRead, since that's the driver PWA's POST
response and drivers have no business receiving read URLs. signed_url is None when
Storage declined to sign — the row is still evidence, just image-unavailable.
EvidenceArtifactWithUrl.title: EvidenceArtifactWithUrl

EvidenceRole.description:
What a capture was taken for. Each value is the stem of the phase column that
records the submitted copy (<value>_artifact_id) and of its anchored hash key
(<value>_sha256), so it is frozen like those names.
EvidenceRole.title: EvidenceRole

ExceptionAnchorRecord.description: Where one action on an exception stands. `pending`/`failed` are debts, never success.
ExceptionAnchorRecord.title: ExceptionAnchorRecord

ExceptionArtifactSummary.description:
One photo of an exception report. Deliberately has no storage key or bucket: bytes
are reached only through the authorised artifact endpoints.
ExceptionArtifactSummary.title: ExceptionArtifactSummary

ExceptionClaimRequest.description:
Claim an exception. take_over must be explicit: replacing a colleague's claim is a
deliberate act, so the default can only ever claim something nobody holds.
ExceptionClaimRequest.title: ExceptionClaimRequest

ExceptionContactMethod.description:
How a dispatcher reached someone while reviewing an exception. NO_CONTACT_YET
has no equivalent here — it recorded the absence of contact, which belongs on
ExceptionReviewOutcome, not a field named for the method of contact.
ExceptionContactMethod.title: ExceptionContactMethod

ExceptionPhoto.description:
One photo of an exception report, tied to the receipt that committed its hash.

`tier` is anchored only when that receipt is intact and commits exactly this artifact
with exactly this hash; otherwise the photo is FreightProof's own record.
ExceptionPhoto.title: ExceptionPhoto

ExceptionPhotoWithUrl.description:
A photo as the dispatcher's detail screen needs it: metadata plus a short-lived signed
URL. signed_url is None when Storage declined to sign; the photo is still recorded.
ExceptionPhotoWithUrl.title: ExceptionPhotoWithUrl

ExceptionReviewOutcome.description:
What a dispatcher concluded when reviewing an exception. LEGACY_REVIEW and
DISPATCHER_AUTHORED are not real choices (see DispatcherReviewOutcome): the first
only back-marks a pre-existing `resolved=true` row as reviewed with no recorded
finding, the second marks a dispatcher's own note as reviewed by its author.
ExceptionReviewOutcome.title: ExceptionReviewOutcome

ExceptionReviewStatus.description:
Where an exception sits in the dispatcher's review workflow. Replaces the old
`resolved: bool`, which couldn't distinguish "not looked at" from "looked at,
still needs a decision".
ExceptionReviewStatus.title: ExceptionReviewStatus

ExpiryBands.description: Separate bands, never cumulative. Further out than 180 days is in none of them.
ExpiryBands.title: ExpiryBands

ExpiryListCard.description: Drivers' licences and vehicles' licence discs: expired or due within `within_days`, or one record's.
ExpiryListCard.title: ExpiryListCard

FacilityMetricsResponse.description: Pulsit corroboration at one precinct, with the precinct's name.

corroboration_rate.description:
Confirmed over CHECKED events. Unwitnessed is deliberately outside the
denominator — "could not check" is not a failure (matches the dispatcher's
"Awaiting Pulsit" state).
corroboration_rate.title: Corroboration Rate

FacilityMetricsResponse.title: FacilityMetricsResponse

FormPreviewCard.description: What "Open trip form" will fill in, shown before the dispatcher clicks (spec D2a, D2b).
FormPreviewCard.title: FormPreviewCard

Grain.description:
How a trend chart groups time. Weeks start Monday (ISO), matching Postgres's
date_trunc('week', ...).
Grain.title: Grain

HandoverConfirmResponse.description: Deliberately thin. The receiver has no further business with this trip.
HandoverConfirmResponse.title: HandoverConfirmResponse

HandoverConsentRequest.description:
The receiver's explicit agreement to a biometric identity check.

POPIA s27(1)(a) exemption relies on proof of what was agreed to: the client sends the
exact wording displayed, the server stores its SHA-256, never the text.
HandoverConsentRequest.title: HandoverConsentRequest

HandoverDeclarationRecord.description: One driver's own capture at a handover (FP-83): what they declared, on their device.
HandoverDeclarationRecord.title: HandoverDeclarationRecord

HandoverResolveRequest.description:
What the receiver typed, for the identity cross-check against the vendor's document.

A body, not query parameters: a name and an ID number in a URL are written to the
access log, proxy logs and platform logs. Defaults stay empty (not required) so a
receiver whose storage was cleared across the vendor redirect can still resolve;
empty simply compares as "nothing typed". Still no session identifier: the server
uses the one it stored itself.
HandoverResolveRequest.title: HandoverResolveRequest

HandoverScanResponse.description:
What a receiver is shown before they confirm anything.

Scoped hard: no driver name, phone number, or other stop on the trip — an unguessable
token is not a reason to hand a scanner the trip's contents.
HandoverScanResponse.title: HandoverScanResponse

HandoverStatusResponse.description: What the driver's step polls while waiting for the receiver to scan.
HandoverStatusResponse.title: HandoverStatusResponse

HandoverTokenResponse.description:
One frame of the driver's rotating QR.

`scan_url` is None exactly when `receiver_opened` is True: no new code to show once
the receiver already holds one.
HandoverTokenResponse.title: HandoverTokenResponse

HandoverVerificationState.description: What the receiver's page shows about its own verification.
HandoverVerificationState.title: HandoverVerificationState

HandoverVerifyResponse.description:
Where to send the receiver next, or why not.

`session_url` is None on every degradation path (quota spent, vendor unreachable, no
document); the client falls back to signing at a lower tier rather than erroring.
HandoverVerifyResponse.title: HandoverVerifyResponse

HistoryCard.description: One driver's or vehicle's trips, counted the way its own page lists them.
HistoryCard.title: HistoryCard

IdentitySnapshot.description:
The incoming driver's fleet verification status as observed. An admin attestation is a
separate fact and never rewrites this status.
IdentitySnapshot.title: IdentitySnapshot

IncidentConfidence.description:
How well-founded the incident is. A client's phone call stays REPORTED until
something independent agrees — it never becomes a system-confirmed theft by itself.
IncidentConfidence.title: IncidentConfidence

IncidentCreate.description:
POST /trips/{trip_id}/incidents. Every fact a report rests on is explicit — the
dispatcher UI fills hijacking defaults (stop the trip, all parcels), the API assumes none.
IncidentCreate.title: IncidentCreate

IncidentDeclarationCreate.description:
What a claim form asks for that FreightProof never captured. Append-only: a
correction is a new declaration, so what was declared when stays on record.
IncidentDeclarationCreate.title: IncidentDeclarationCreate

IncidentDeclarationRecord.description:
Police and notification facts the operator typed in after the event. Always the
Declared tier: FreightProof did not capture any of it, so the pack never presents it
as if it had.
IncidentDeclarationRecord.title: IncidentDeclarationRecord

IncidentExternalAction.description:
Something done outside FreightProof that the dispatcher records. FreightProof records
these responses; it never performs them (docs/scope-boundaries.md §0).
IncidentExternalAction.title: IncidentExternalAction

IncidentOutcome.description:
What the investigation established. Kept apart from IncidentStatus so closing never
has to pretend cargo was recovered — INCONCLUSIVE is a legitimate way to close.
IncidentOutcome.title: IncidentOutcome

IncidentPin.description:
One located report on the incident map (chart 3.6). Deliberately nothing about the
person: no driver name, phone or id. A pin is where a named driver was, so it carries only
what the dispatcher needs to open the report (POPIA).
IncidentPin.title: IncidentPin

IncidentRead.description: One incident in a list: enough to triage without opening it.
IncidentRead.title: IncidentRead

IncidentStatus.description:
Where the investigation is. Independent of Trip.status (a trip can close while a
shortage investigation stays open) and of each exception's review_status.
IncidentStatus.title: IncidentStatus

IncidentSummary.description:
The key times an adjuster or detective reads first, derived from the critical
exceptions. Built only when the trip has at least one.
IncidentSummary.title: IncidentSummary

IncidentType.description:
What an incident investigates. An exception is one observation; an incident is the
investigation several observations can belong to. Breakdowns are deliberately absent:
out of MVP scope (Tim, 20 Oct 2026) — MECHANICAL stays an exception.
IncidentType.title: IncidentType

IncidentUpdateKind.description:
One entry on an incident's append-only ledger. The status, confidence, owner and
outcome columns on Incident are caches rebuilt from these, never edited directly.
IncidentUpdateKind.title: IncidentUpdateKind

InvestigationEntryRecord.description: One entry of an incident's append-only ledger, as recorded by a dispatcher.
InvestigationEntryRecord.title: InvestigationEntryRecord

InvestigationRecord.description:
An incident the operator investigated: who reported what and when, how sure, what was
affected, every follow-up, and what it established — or that it was still open. Declared
tier throughout: the operator recorded all of it; FreightProof captured none of it.
InvestigationRecord.title: InvestigationRecord

LaneMetricsResponse.description: One origin -> destination lane, with both precinct names.
LaneMetricsResponse.title: LaneMetricsResponse

LaneRisk.description: Charts 2.4 and 6.3: one origin -> destination lane over the period.
LaneRisk.title: LaneRisk

LateEvidenceDetailRead.description:
Dispatcher view: the retained typed evidence, its commitment and scoped artifact URLs,
so acknowledgement follows an actual review.
LateEvidenceDetailRead.title: LateEvidenceDetailRead

LateEvidenceRecord.description:
Evidence a driver captured in an earlier custody period, retained for review (FP-83).
It never completed a phase; `payload_sha256` is a local commitment, not a Hedera receipt.
LateEvidenceRecord.title: LateEvidenceRecord

LatenessBand.description:
Chart 2.2. Early and on time are separate so the strict on-time rule doesn't hide
trips that left far ahead of an unrealistic plan.
LatenessBand.title: LatenessBand

LatenessBar.description: Chart 2.2: how many trips fell in one lateness band over the whole period.
LatenessBar.title: LatenessBar

LinehaulResponse.description:
Driver-facing single document — vehicle, driver, consolidated unit count.

Deliberately excludes per-parcel data and per-stop breakdown — the driver
must never see contents or per-parcel detail, only a consolidated unit
count (theft-risk rule, 2026-06-24 coordination note).
LinehaulResponse.title: LinehaulResponse

LocationPingBatch.description: The request body — one or more fixes for a single trip.
LocationPingBatch.title: LocationPingBatch

LocationPingBatchResult.description: What the batch write actually stored, so the PWA can clear exactly those entries.
LocationPingBatchResult.title: LocationPingBatchResult

LocationPingCreate.description: One position fix as the device recorded it.
LocationPingCreate.title: LocationPingCreate

ManifestResponse.description: Full per-parcel manifest — dispatcher only. Never sent to the driver PWA.
ManifestResponse.title: ManifestResponse

NeedsReview.description: A trip's exceptions waiting for a dispatcher's review, by severity (the dashboard's split).
NeedsReview.title: NeedsReview

Observation.description:
A factual, rule-generated sentence. States what the record shows, never a
conclusion about fault — FreightProof records, it does not adjudicate.
Observation.title: Observation

OperatingCost.description: Estimated operating cost of the period's costed trips, by what drives it.
OperatingCost.title: OperatingCost

OverridePhaseRequest.description:
POST /trips/{trip_id}/phases/{phase_event_id}/override body. Same required-note
rationale as CancelTripRequest — a dispatcher bypassing driver-attested evidence must state why.
OverridePhaseRequest.title: OverridePhaseRequest

OverridesBucket.description:
Chart 5.2: every step of the closed-trip set, and how many a dispatcher overrode. The
driver view's override_rate definition.
OverridesBucket.title: OverridesBucket

PPManifestPreviewResponse.description:
GET /trips/pp-manifest-preview. Read-only. snapshot_sha256 is sent back with the
create request, so what the dispatcher reviewed is what gets locked (spec §10.2).
PPManifestPreviewResponse.title: PPManifestPreviewResponse

PPManifestRef.description: A trip's PP manifest key plus a display label (spec §6). Null on trips without one.
PPManifestRef.title: PPManifestRef

PPManifestSnapshotRead.description:
The H0 snapshot as the dispatcher's manifest panel shows it (FP-281 §7.3).

Built from the stored snapshot by the same helper the preview uses, so the panel's
creation-time lines and totals are exactly the ones the dispatcher reviewed. The
stored JSON itself, which also holds receiver names and contact numbers, stays in
Postgres for verification and is never sent.
PPManifestSnapshotRead.title: PPManifestSnapshotRead

PPManifestWaybillLine.description: Dispatcher-only line detail, as on the manifest panel today.
PPManifestWaybillLine.title: PPManifestWaybillLine

PPWaybillSummary.description: Wizard-time validation summary. Never the raw PP payload.
PPWaybillSummary.title: PPWaybillSummary

PageView.description:
What the dispatcher has on screen when they ask (B45, Stage 4b): the open tab, its Period and its View by.
So "what do these figures tell us?" is answered for the period on screen instead of asking for one. A period
the question names itself still wins. Holds no personal data.
PageView.title: PageView

ParcelFinding.description:
What a dispatcher established about one affected parcel. There is no "stolen" and no
"no scan recorded" here: a missing scan-in is a scan fact read from Parcel, shown beside
the finding, and a parcel with no finding yet is simply not established.
ParcelFinding.title: ParcelFinding

ParticipationActionRef.description: An opaque reference to one of this driver's own immutable actions.
ParticipationActionRef.title: ParticipationActionRef

PatternBar.description: One bar of a busy-pattern chart: an hour, weekday, date or month.
PatternBar.title: PatternBar

PatternSet.description:
Always complete and in clock/calendar order: 24 hours (0-23), 7 weekdays (Monday = 0),
31 dates (1-31), 12 months (1-12). Never sorted by size.
PatternSet.title: PatternSet

PeriodEcho.description:
The period the answer covers, as the server resolved it. "All time" comes back with
its real first day, so the page can say which dates it is showing.
PeriodEcho.title: PeriodEcho

PhaseEventRead.description:
One entry in a trip's committed phase plan, as served to the UI.

NOT built with model_validate() — stop_sequence needs a TripStop join and
step_recipe is derived, so use from_event() and pass the map. Building this
from the ORM object alone would silently produce stop_sequence=None on every
row, which the dispatcher renders as "no stop" rather than as an error.
PhaseEventRead.title: PhaseEventRead

PhaseType.description:
One entry in a trip's committed phase plan; plan LENGTH is
data generated per trip, so this enum's cardinality is not the phase count of
any one trip — a type can appear more than once on a multi-stop route.
PhaseType.title: PhaseType

PlanBand.description:
Chart 2.5's nine columns, left to right: finished early (furthest first), exactly on plan,
ran over (nearest first), so the histogram reads as one line from early to late.
PlanBand.title: PlanBand

PlanSpread.description:
Chart 2.5, whole period: how far each trip's actual time was from planned. Medians
are positive minutes on both sides ("typically 40 min early"), never negative.
PlanSpread.title: PlanSpread

PrecinctCreateBody.description:
Fields an admin dispatcher submits when mapping a new precinct.

principal_organization_id is deliberately absent — ownership is injected from the
caller's JWT, not accepted from the client (SEC-PRECINCT-1).
PrecinctCreateBody.title: PrecinctCreateBody

PrecinctDetailResponse.description: Extended shape returned by GET /precincts/{id}, with full change history and receipts.
PrecinctDetailResponse.title: PrecinctDetailResponse

PrecinctUpdateBody.description:
Fields an admin dispatcher may change via PATCH /precincts/{id}; only supplied
fields apply (model_dump(exclude_unset=True)). principal_organization_id is absent:
ownership is not transferable.

Omissible is not the same as nullable: `Optional[X]` means the column accepts an
explicit null; a bare `X = Field(default=None)` means omissible but not nullable.
Only `address` and `geofence_polygon` are genuinely nullable on the Precinct model — the rest would otherwise
raise NotNullViolation at flush as a 500 instead of a 422.
test_patch_schema_nullability_matches_the_precinct_model pins this against the model.
PrecinctUpdateBody.title: PrecinctUpdateBody

ProblemStepCount.description: Chart 3.4: the linked step's phase type, or "unlinked".
ProblemStepCount.title: ProblemStepCount

ProblemTypeCount.description:
Chart 3.3: only (type, source) pairs that happened, so a type nothing creates never
sits at a reassuring zero.
ProblemTypeCount.title: ProblemTypeCount

ProblemsPerTripBucket.description: Chart 3.1. Info is counted but not drawn: nothing raises it today.
ProblemsPerTripBucket.title: ProblemsPerTripBucket

PublicPackSeal.description:
Everything needed to check a pack's seal and nothing about the trip itself — safe
to show to whoever holds a forwarded PDF.
PublicPackSeal.title: PublicPackSeal

PunctualityBucket.description: Chart 2.1. Strict: on or before the plan, no grace window.
PunctualityBucket.title: PunctualityBucket

PushPlatform.description: The native shell a push token came from; the sender picks the FCM/APNs path by it.
PushPlatform.title: PushPlatform

PushTokenRegistration.description: What the driver app sends after the OS hands it a token (Capacitor `registration`).
PushTokenRegistration.title: PushTokenRegistration

QueueBucket.description: Chart 4.2: critical problems still waiting at the end of the bucket (or now, if sooner).
QueueBucket.title: QueueBucket

ReceiverSignoffBucket.description:
Chart 5.7: attested sign-off steps of the closed-trip set, and how many the receiver
confirmed by scanning the QR.
ReceiverSignoffBucket.title: ReceiverSignoffBucket

RecordChange.description:
A driver or vehicle master-record edit made while the trip was running —
adjusters read these as possible collusion signals.
RecordChange.title: RecordChange

RecordRef.description:
One record an answer showed: what the next question's "him" or "the first horse" can mean.

The browser sends these back with the conversation. They are never trusted: a tool that receives one
re-loads the record by id, scoped to the caller's organisation, so a forged id is simply not found.
The label only names the record to the model, so it is length-capped like any typed text.
RecordRef.title: RecordRef

ReplaceSubstitutionRequest.description:
Cancels the old request and creates a fresh one atomically: the complete new
arrangement, with its own ``reason``, plus why it replaces the old one.
ReplaceSubstitutionRequest.title: ReplaceSubstitutionRequest

ResponseStep.description: One step of the hijacking response guide, derived from what was recorded.
ResponseStep.title: ResponseStep

ReviewAgeBand.description: Chart 4.1: how long critical problems have waited for review.
ReviewAgeBand.title: ReviewAgeBand

ReviewOutcomeCount.description: Chart 4.4: reviews of any severity concluded in the period, per real outcome.
ReviewOutcomeCount.title: ReviewOutcomeCount

ReviewQueueCard.description: The Exceptions page's queue in numbers: every exception waiting for review, on any trip.
ReviewQueueCard.title: ReviewQueueCard

RiskyTimeBlock.description: Chart 3.5. Shares are of the period's totals across all four blocks, divided once here.
RiskyTimeBlock.title: RiskyTimeBlock

RosterCard.description: How many drivers, horses, trailers and depots there are (coverage audit item 4).
RosterCard.title: RosterCard

SealCheck.description: One vehicle's seal declaration at a handover (contract "Types" and seal rules).
SealCheck.title: SealCheck

SealCondition.description:
The seal's physical condition as the driver finds it at arrival. Stored as a
plain String, like every enum here, so adding a value needs no migration.
SealCondition.title: SealCondition

SealNumberSource.description:
How the seal number on a departure or arrival row was entered on the phone.

Recorded, never anchored: it describes the capture, not the seal, and keeping it out
of the payload leaves the departure and arrival anchor contracts unchanged.
SealNumberSource.title: SealNumberSource

SiteActivity.description: Chart 1.6: attested pickups and deliveries at one site over the period.
SiteActivity.title: SiteActivity

SubstitutionCompletionBlocker.description: Declaration order IS the contract's fixed precedence when several checks fail.

TripAttentionResponse.description:
A trip's unreviewed exceptions split the two ways the dashboard ranks them: by
severity, so a critical outranks any number of warnings, and by claim, so a dispatcher
can see which ones nobody has taken on. A claimed exception is still unreviewed (FP-280),
so critical + warning + info always equals needs_review_count, claimed or not.

Explicit ids, never "every warning on the trip": the dispatcher confirms exactly the
rows they saw, so a warning raised after the page loaded is never swept into a
review nobody looked at. One review is still written per row.

TripExceptionListItem.description:
Compact row for the review queue and history list.

Built explicitly from a (TripException, Trip, phase_type, stop_sequence) tuple in
the service layer, not via model_validate on the bare ORM object — the trip
reference/status and the phase/stop labels all come from the same org-scoping join,
not from TripException's own columns. See exception_service._to_list_item.
TripExceptionListItem.title: TripExceptionListItem

TripExceptionReviewRequest.description:
The dispatcher's review action.

The narrow request keeps the reviewer and timestamp server-owned rather than
accepting either as client input.

`contact_method` is required but nullable, with no default — a caller MUST decide
whether contact happened at all (unlike `review_outcome`, which has no "not
applicable" option), and an explicit `null` records "reviewed without contacting
anyone" (e.g. the evidence alone settled it) rather than a caller having forgotten
the field.

`take_over` lets a dispatcher take over a colleague's claim and review in one step
(FP-280 soft claim); false by default, so a stale page never overrides a claim it
didn't show.
TripExceptionReviewRequest.title: TripExceptionReviewRequest

TripFormParams.description:

TripFormParams.title: TripFormParams

TripFromPPManifestRequest.description:
POST /trips/from-pp-manifest (spec §10.2).

Cargo is never accepted from the client — the server pulls it. Precincts are used
only for a hub the manifest could not link; planned times override the manifest's.
Times must carry a zone (AwareDatetime): the lock normalises to UTC, and a zone-less
value could not be normalised honestly.
TripFromPPManifestRequest.title: TripFromPPManifestRequest

get.description:
Report whether this instance can actually reach Postgres and Redis.

Probes run concurrently, so a degraded answer costs one timeout, not two.
The session is read-only so nothing commits on the way out.

Answers 503 when either dependency is unreachable — the status code is
what an orchestrator/load balancer reads without being taught this
response shape, so a degraded instance doesn't keep getting traffic.
